title.narrative: CI Bolivia (2022-25): Forest conservation and biodiversity
CI Bolivia (2022-25): Skogsförvaltning och biologisk mångfald

description.narrative: Att förbättra landskapsskötsel och skydd mot skogsavverkning i tre utvalda bolivianska regioner. Målet är att upprätthålla funktionaliteten och den biologiska mångfalden i naturlandskap och skogar.
To improve landscape management and forest protection in three selected Bolivian regions. The objective is to maintain the functionality and biodiversity of natural landscapes and forests.

The overal objectives is to: Maintain the functionality and biodiversity of natural landscapes and forests at three governance levels: the Department of Pando, the Municipality of Sorata, and the District of Zongo in La Paz Municipality, by creating and strengthening conservation schemes, strengthening subnational governments and IPLC leaders capacities, making accessible quality information to improve decision making, enhancing IPLC voice to influence public policies, and developing learning processes for establishing networks and exchanges among the three governance levels.
Project main outcomes:
a) Enhanced and inclusive conservation, restoration, sustainable management and use of forests and biodiversity, both within and outside protected areas, including wildfire prevention and implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts:
- Strengthening the capacities of IPLCs, local authorities, and key stakeholders at different governance levels (Departmental, Municipal, and District) to manage their territories and conserve biodiversity. This will include capacity building in biodiversity conservation programs and the consolidation of networks for conservation.
- Supporting the creation of conservation mosaics in at least 288,000 hectares (ha) of high biodiversity value, which includes 70,000 ha acquire a new conservation status, 73,000 ha improve their management, and 145,000 has engaged in Conservation Agreements (CAs).
- Promoting public policies at the national and subnational level for sustainable management of conservation areas, biodiversity conservation, and climate change adaptation, which includes implementing a Municipal Protected Area network at national level, supporting the development of strategies for Protected Areas (PAs) management, territorial planning, and strategies for results-based cooperation mechanism in Pando, and climate change adaptation in Sorata.
- Encouraging greater transparency, improved access to environmental information, and enhanced participation of indigenous and local communities and civil society in environmental decision-making, to make informed decisions and use the information to raise awareness through a communication campaign in Pando.
b) Broad participation of women in decision-making and activities related to the environment, climate change, and sustainable production:
- Increasing womens participation in decision-making and activities related to the environment, climate change, sustainable production, and capacity building to actively participate in conservation and sustainable development.

Results: Main achievements to highlight from the work 2023 of the project are listed below. These results are primarily linked to the SEEU logical frameworks, Outcome 1 Inclusive improvement and conservation, restoration, sustainable management and use of forests and biodiversity, both inside and outside protected areas, including the prevention of forest fires and the implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation measures, and Outcome 4 Broad participation of women in decision making and activities related to the environment, climate change and sustainable production: Creation of the Gran Manupare Municipal Protected Area, in Pando department (452,639 hectares). Sustainable management of 5,115 hectares through Zongo Conservation Agreements (exceeding the initial goal in terms of the number of new protected hectares). 26 women leaders have participated in capacity building processes, including three from Conservation International's Women Leaders Program. Formation and consolidation of the Network for Protected Areas with Municipalities and Indigenous Native Peasant Autonomies. Completion of a comprehensive registry that includes 69 municipalities with a total of 138 Municipal Protected Areas, as well as three Indigenous Native Peasant Protected Areas (APIOC), totaling 141 Subnational Protected Areas. Technical support to the updating of PLUS Pando (Departmental Land Use Plan), with Pando Departmental Government (GAD Pando), through the Secretariat for the Integral Management of Mother Earth (SDGIMT). PLUS Pando is considered a key instrument to ensure a future with a strong conservation focus, to avoid increasing deforestation rates. Strengthening the management of the Bruno Racua Wildlife Reserve, in close collaboration with GAD Pando. Initially, a diagnosis of the situation of the reserve was carried out together with the Secretariat of Mother Earth to initiate the necessary actions. The initial support also included equipping forest rangers and support improvement of key reserve infrastructure. In terms of visibility and communication, focus have been on highlighting key achievements such as the creation of the Gran Manupare protected area communicating news related to the Nature Reporting Award as well as actions in preparation for the PLUS Pando participatory process.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
